claims.note: Headline and description assert only what the repository states: local SQLite capture of Claude Code sessions, report rendering, and byte-identity as the author's claim ("byte-identical every time") rather than as a measured fact of this review.
Repository API returns 24 stars, 0 forks, MIT licence; crates.io API returns 158 total downloads. Both read 2026-10-19 and quoted as adoption signals, explicitly not usage evidence.

audited.xyz report dated April 07, 2026 records the update_environment_variables mutation, the NODE_OPTIONS proof of concept against Claude Code 2.1.92, and its own Low severity plus the remote-worker-only attack-surface limitation. The article carries version, date and severity with the claim.
README technical-details line states 16-crate engine, 16 of 17 crates published, 21 lifecycle hooks, 12 MCP tools; the five slash commands are listed in the Get started section.

Record/store/report/reuse stages follow the README architecture section: transcript always on with no API calls, 21 hook events, optional proxy/OTLP, one local file per run, JSON/HTML/Markdown output, 12 read-only MCP tools.

Inference from the stated render path: if rendering is a pure function of stored rows with no clock, network or model input, then determinism is reproducibility from the store and not authenticity of the store. The README makes no tamper-evidence claim, so the article attributes no such guarantee and states the implication openly.

Counts and denominator read directly from the shipped artifact on 2026-10-19T00:21Z: summary.error_results 60, validation.items[0].runs 373, rework.hotspots 96 entries, summary.tools 17 entries, scope.session_count 7, summary.runs 7, summary.transcript_turns 9132 over 2026-05-04T19:07Z..2026-05-18T06:06Z. The README FAQ independently says 'a captured window of 7 real sessions'.

The 60-error figure and the vendor's statement that the agent's own summary never mentioned it are both in the README (Why developers use it); the same README credits it to 'one real captured session' while the shipped artifact records error_results=60 under scope.session_count=7, and the article names that conflict and follows the artifact.

Read from capture.channels in the shipped artifact: hooks, events, spans, requests, file_history and provider_cost_usd are 'not_recorded'; plan_docs and raw_logs are 'not_observed'; transcripts is 'partial' with 629 dangling parent(s) and 136 unpaired tool_use/tool_result over 9,132 turns. The README's blanket 'not_observed' wording is contradicted by the artifact, so the article follows the artifact.

99-of-101 result and the exact mechanism (--locked install from crates.io, ingest shipped transcripts, jq -S normalization deleting integrity.source_db_hash and report.id, then diff) are both in tests/verify.sh and the verification page.

Scopes the determinism evidence honestly: 99 fields matched after excluding the two documented per-ingest fields; the script is vendor-authored, runs on a vendor fixture, and is repeatable by third parties but is not a third-party audit. The article says this rather than calling it independent.
The six checks are enumerated in wiki/human-md/verification.md, which also states the suite cannot re-prove the 699 private tests or verify genuine refusal of MCP writes.
Same README carries 699 tests in Technical details and 716 tests in the 0.3.0 status paragraph; both are quoted only to flag the inconsistency, and neither is used as support for a capability claim.

Install commands are reproduced verbatim from the README Get started section, including the manual cargo install step for bar-hook, bar-mcp and bar-observatory that the README discloses as a plugin gap.

Author-side characterisation of tracing/evaluation platforms by their aggregation and dashboard purpose, linked to this site's existing coverage. No vendor metric, star count or benchmark is quoted for any compared tool.

Author-side positioning of tool categories, not a measured comparison: tracing platforms are characterised by their aggregation purpose, memory tools by model compression, permission checkers by static config review. No competitor metric or vendor claim is quoted.

Positioning statement about the slot Bar Observatory occupies (per-run diffable local record) and its weakness (a local file is only as trustworthy as its host). This is analysis grounded in the recorded pipeline, not a benchmark against other tools.

All figures read 2026-10-19: 24 stars, 0 forks, MIT, created 2026-08-12, last push 2026-08-27 from the repo API; 158 downloads and 0.3.0 published 2026-08-27 from crates.io; release list stops at v0.2.1 (2026-08-20). Release lag is stated as an observation, not a defect.

README lists 12 read-only MCP tools; the verification page states that genuine write refusal is not re-proved from outside. The article therefore treats read-only as intended design pending the reader's own test.

Consequence of the reproducibility-versus-authenticity distinction established in the pipeline section: signed records or third-party attestation are a different control that this tool does not claim to provide.

Every listed URL was fetched on 2026-10-19, including the shipped example report added in this correction round (S8, 71,402 bytes, sha256 27d6c5b9...); each is the page actually read, not a search result.
Restates the measurement date and the audit's scope (Claude Code 2.1.92 remote-worker mode, Low severity) so the preceding links cannot be read as a security assessment of Bar Observatory itself.
